newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland says NATO-Russia deal will lower tensions.
newsitem.headline: Poland says NATO-Russia deal will lower tensions.

text.p: Poland welcomed Wednesday's deal between Russia and NATO on new peaceful cooperation, saying work on the western military alliance's eastward expansion would now proceed in a better climate.
"Poland welcomes the agreement..., which is a basis for cooperation and lowering tensions in Europe," Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati told reporters.

"It (the deal) removes one of the important elements of dispute.... Although the calendar of NATO expansion would have been implemented regardless of the agreement, it will now proceed in a better climate, a better atmosphere," he added.
NATO has promised to invite a first batch of countries which once belonged to the defunct Warsaw Pact to start negotiations on membership at a summit in Madrid summit in July.
Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary, leaders of economic and democratic reforms in eastern Europe, are expected to be among the first invitees.
Rosati said the deal, struck in Moscow by Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and NATO Secretary General Javier Solana, should not infringe on the rights of new NATO members.
"The agreement should not create a second-class membership category and must in no way provide for delaying the alliance's expansion," he said.

Details of the agreement, now submitted for consideration to NATO governments and to Russian President Boris Yeltsin, were not immediately released and it was not clear if all differences had been fully resolved.
Russia has opposed moving NATO military infrastructure closer to its borders, saying this would pose a threat to its national security.
Solana and Primakov said their agreement opened the way for Moscow and the Western alliance to sign the security deal on May 27 in Paris.
